title: Finding
description: One vulnerability finding. Written append-only as workspace/findings/<id>.json. The `status` flag + `history` are what drive the streaming convergence and the reproduction feedback loop.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. sha1(track + vuln_class + sink.file + sink.line). Same logical bug must hash to the same id so re-runs do not duplicate.

correlation_id.description: Groups findings that share a root cause (e.g. one tainted source reaching many sinks). Used by convergence for de-dup.

track.description: A/F/H = web data-flow, blackbox injection, or web3 fund-flow; B/G/I = web logic/authz, blackbox logic, or web3 access-control; Android tracks: M manifest/permissions, L component types/IPC, K cross-component sink chains, W WebView, N native/passive zero-click, J legacy Android Intent/deep-link.

vuln_class.description: Kebab-case class tag, e.g. sql-injection, command-injection, xss, deserialization, idor, broken-access-control, auth-bypass, business-logic, use-after-free, toctou-race, crypto-misuse, info-leak, dos, misconfiguration, supply-chain. See .agents/skills/_shared/METHODOLOGY.md section 7 for the full tag list.

defect_shape.description: Which of the two defect shapes this is. flow = attacker-influenced value reaches a dangerous operation (source/propagation/sink must all be stated). missing_control = a required check is absent from a reachable path (missing_control must be stated). A class does not decide the shape; the evidence does.

cwe.description: e.g. CWE-89. Pulled from Semgrep rule metadata when available.

severity_estimate.description: Producer's first guess. Triage may revise after reproduction.

description.description: What makes this attacker-controlled (e.g. GET param).

flow.description: Ordered source->sink path. Each hop is a step the taint/reasoning crossed.

missing_control.description: Required for defect_shape=missing_control. States WHICH control is absent and from WHICH reachable path - the absence shape has no taint to show, so this is its evidence.

control.description: The control that should exist, e.g. 'ownership check on the loaded object', 'capability check current_user_can(edit_posts)', 'CSRF token verification', 'lock around read-then-debit'.

expected_at.description: file:line (or symbol) locations where the control should sit, e.g. the handler, the service method, the middleware layer.

unguarded_path.description: The concrete reachable path that reaches the privileged operation without the control: entry point -> ... -> operation.

actor.description: The actor who can take the path, e.g. 'unauthenticated', 'any authenticated user', 'contributor', 'tenant B user'.

evidence.description: Why the control is genuinely absent on this path - which callers were enumerated, which layer was checked, where the equivalent check does exist for comparison.

reachability.description: Who can trigger this, with what privilege. 'Reachable' is proven by an entry point plus a call chain, never assumed from a route name. Required before a finding may become confirmed.

entry_point.description: The externally reachable trigger, e.g. 'POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=find_posts', 'queue consumer onMessage', 'exported Activity com.x.Y'.

min_privilege.description: Lowest privilege that reaches the defect, e.g. 'unauthenticated', 'subscriber', 'any tenant member', 'local user in the docker group'.

pre_auth.description: True when reachable with no authentication at all; null when not applicable to this target type.

call_chain.description: Ordered symbols or file:line hops from the entry point to the sink / privileged operation. This is the reachability proof.

preconditions.description: What has to be true for the defect to exist. Keeps a non-default-configuration bug from being reported as if it fired out of the box.

default_configuration.description: True when the preconditions hold in the default/vendor-shipped configuration; false when a non-default setting is required; null when undetermined.

required_settings.description: Exact non-default settings, plugins, build flags, roles, or deployment modes the defect needs.

primitive.description: The capability actually proven, and the honest ceiling of it. Guards against over-packaging: an unproven escalation is recorded in ruled_out, never in the title.

escalation_ceiling.description: The highest impact actually proven, stated as a bound - e.g. 'read-only, self-owned objects only', 'DoS only: no control over the freed chunk contents', 'authz bypass to contributor-level publish; no path to admin found'.

ruled_out.description: Escalations that were attempted and did NOT work, with the reason. Absence of an attempt is not a rule-out.

assets_affected.description: Which assets from the threat model this touches, e.g. 'session secrets', 'other users' draft content', 'funds', 'integrity of the permission model', 'availability of the API worker pool'.

sanitizers_seen.description: Validation/escaping encountered on the path. Empty = no sanitization.

evidence.description: LLM reasoning for why this is (or isn't) exploitable.

status.description: Lifecycle. candidate -> cross_validated -> reproduced -> official_review -> confirmed. A disproved reproduction is false_positive; reproduced behavior that official/vendor evidence identifies as expected, unsupported, a documented hazard, or application misconfiguration is not_product_vulnerability.

poc.description: The EXACT reproducing request(s) - the full probe.py/curl command(s) incl. method, URL, headers, cookies/jar, and payload, so a human can copy-paste and re-run it. For IDOR include both identities' requests.

env.description: Which warm target env was used.

reliability.description: How repeatable the reproduction is, e.g. '10/10 runs', '3/50 runs - race window is narrow'. Required honesty for races, TOCTOU, and heap-state-dependent bugs.

instrumentation_only.description: True when the observation so far exists only under a sanitizer, debug assertion, patched build, or diagnostic probe. Such an observation is a lead, not a finding, until stock_replay succeeds.

stock_replay.description: Result of replaying on the exact stock/uninstrumented build or release artifact, including its version/build id. Empty means not yet attempted.

response.description: Key evidence from the live response that proves the bug (status, decisive snippet, timing, canary HIT).

poc_script.description: Full, self-contained Python source of a poc.py that reproduces THIS vuln when run. Web PoCs normally use requests; Android PoCs invoke the repository's emulator-only probe harness. Saved verbatim to report/<id>/poc.py.

history.description: Audit trail. Every stage that touches this finding appends an entry. Makes the feedback loop debuggable.

official_review.description: Mandatory product-boundary review after reproduction and before confirmation. Terminal verdicts must identify the exact product version, assess whether the precondition is default/vendor-generated, and compare the reproduced behavior with official vendor documentation, API contracts, security guidance, default templates/samples, source comments/tests, advisories, release notes, patches, and vendor-owned issue discussions.

checked.description: True only after the official/vendor evidence review was actually performed.

verdict.description: product_vulnerability = reproduced behavior violates the supported product's stated/default security boundary; known_vulnerability = official advisory/CVE/patch already identifies the same bug; documented_hazard = official guidance explicitly describes the exact unsafe ordering/configuration and its mitigation; expected_behavior = official contract/tests intentionally require the behavior; application_misconfiguration = impact exists only because app-authored configuration or a sink creates it contrary to defaults/guidance; unsupported_scenario = reproduction depends on an explicitly unsupported deployment or mode; inconclusive = official evidence is insufficient or contradictory.

sources.description: Official/vendor materials examined so far. A terminal confirmed/not_product_vulnerability verdict is additionally gated by write_finding.py and must include at least one public URL to official documentation, security guidance/advisory, release/patch note, or vendor-owned repository issue/discussion. Local source paths and GitHub blob/tree/raw source URLs are supporting evidence only and cannot pass the gate alone.

rationale.description: Exact comparison between the reproduction, supported/default configuration, documented contract, and vendor guidance. State why the behavior is or is not a product vulnerability.

default_configuration.description: Whether the vulnerable preconditions occur in a vendor-generated or default supported configuration; null when not determinable.

disclosure.description: Set by convergence only after official_review says the behavior is a real product vulnerability. Novel classification additionally requires an exact-match public-history review across source history, upstream head/release code, vendor issues/PRs, and advisories/releases.

status.description: novel = no matching public issue, PR, commit, patch, advisory, CVE, release note, or changelog entry was found after the public_history search ladder; known = any exact public vendor match exists, even without a CVE/security label; inconclusive = unsure

references.description: Exact public vendor issue, PR, commit, patch, advisory, CVE, release, or changelog URLs. A matching public source-level fix is known disclosure even when it has no CVE or security label.

rationale.description: why classified novel/known (what the search showed)

public_history.description: Mandatory search evidence before status=novel. Record exact anchors and the concrete searches/comparisons performed; absence of a CVE or advisory alone is never enough.

upstream_repository.description: Canonical public upstream repository HTTPS URL.

exact_anchors.description: At least two exact patch fingerprints, such as file+symbol, helper/flag, rejection reason, distinctive literal, or protocol invariant.

source_history.description: git log -S/-G commands/results, GitHub commit-history/API URLs, blame/history checks, or exact public commit searches for the affected path.

vendor_issues_prs.description: Vendor repository issue/PR searches using exact symbols and semantic variants, including closed/merged items and linked backports.

advisories_releases.description: Vendor advisories, CVEs, release notes, changelogs, and servicing/backport searches.

head_or_release_comparison.description: Exact comparison of the tested version with current upstream main and applicable supported release branch. Any matching public hardening diff makes the finding known.

exploit.description: Deep exploitation result from agent D (only for critical confirmed findings that passed the official/vendor product-boundary gate)

constraints.description: honest bounds, e.g. only single-token commands

hypothesis_id.description: id of the HYPOTHESES.json hypothesis this finding validates, if any

reanalysis_count.description: how many times this finding bounced to needs_reanalysis; capped so it isn't re-verified forever
